messages.author: 19bd56a3837861ad
messages.subject: Can't find packages: Shiny Server
parts:
Hi there, I am not very strong at using Ubuntu/Linux so apologies in advance

I have made an app which runs fine locally and uses the packages ShinyDash and lme4

My current set up:

in Server.R I have

library(shiny)
library(lme4)

and in ui.R I have 

library(shiny)
library(ShinyDash)

When I run the app over the server I get "ERROR: there is no package called â€˜ShinyDashâ€™" in the browser. 
If I put library(ShinyDash) into server.R I can see that the lme4 package loads fine but again an issue with ShinyDash..

I have tried to install both packages system wide by running sudo R and installing packages through there
I know that shiny server runs as user shiny so thought perhaps it is something to do with shiny user not being to find the package but I thought I may have got round this by installing "ShinyDash" system-wide..
Also, you have to install ShinyDash from github https://github.com/trestletech/ShinyDash so is it an issue with not using the traditional install.packages() methods?

Any ideas?

Thanks!

messages.author: 19bd56a3837861ad
messages.subject: Re: Can't find packages: Shiny Server
parts:
Okay so I think I'm getting closer - using path.package(), I can see that lme4 is installed in /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/" but ShinyDash is installed in "/home/emma/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.0/ShinyDash"
I presume I need to get ShinyDash to install in the same location as lme4 and this will solve my problem (shiny user can see the /usr/local/... library but not the /home/emma/... one?) 

Am I correct and if so how do I install ShinyDash here? :)

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Can't find packages: Shiny Server
parts:
sudo R is not enough, you need sudo su - -c R

The extra stuff is needed for R to truly think of you as the root user, and thus forget about your personal R library dir. This is way too tricky, perhaps a helper script is in order.

I found one way around this by just copying the folder from the /home/emma/... library to the /usr/local/... library which worked - hurray!

I'm sure there's a more elegant way to install it in the correct place first time though...
